implemented_requirements.requirement: Provide multiple strands of text for each puzzle
implemented_requirements.evidence: puzzles.js defines arrays of strands for four puzzles.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Allow player to combine strands to form words/phrases
implemented_requirements.evidence: Strands can be selected/deselected via onStrandClick and onTrayItemClick in game.js, building a tray that concatenates the texts.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Verify that the concatenated strands match a valid answer
implemented_requirements.evidence: merge() in game.js normalises the tray text and checks it against currentPuzzle.answers.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Give feedback on successful and failed merges
implemented_requirements.evidence: FeedbackMessages pools and showFeedback()/logFeedback() are used after each merge attempt.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Detect puzzle completion when all answers are found
implemented_requirements.evidence: complete() is called when this.found.size equals the number of answers.
updateProgress() and updateStats() update DOM elements with counts.
hint() searches for a decomposition of an unfound answer and highlights the first strand.
SoundKit class is instantiated and its methods are called on clicks, successes, errors, and completion.

critical_issues: index.html is empty (placeholder "FILENAME"), so none of the DOM elements referenced in game.js (e.g., #strandBoard, #mergeTray, #feedbackMessage) exist. The application cannot initialise or render.
The IDs used in StrandsGame.dom (strandBoard, mergeTray, etc.) do not match the class names defined in styles.css (e.g., .strand-board). Without matching markup the UI will not function.
No script tags are shown to load game.js, puzzles.js, or main.js, meaning the JavaScript would never execute even if the HTML were present.
Missing <script> imports and CSS link in the HTML prevents the game from being runnable in a browser.
judge.summary: The codebase implements the core game mechanics—strand selection, merge validation, feedback, hints, and completion detection—fulfilling the functional requirements of a Strands‑style word‑segmentation puzzle. However, the absence of a functional HTML entry point and mismatched DOM identifiers make the program non‑executable as provided. Because the application cannot be launched or interacted with, the overall submission fails the acceptance criteria despite strong internal logic.
